paragraphs.source_en: It was published again in Istanbul as a pamphlet in 1912. In this work, Akcura argued that the political project of Ottomanism—to create an Ottoman nation based on a union of the empire’s diverse peoples through loyalty to the dynasty—had failed in part due to the rise of nationalism.™ Pan-Islamism, the political unification of all Muslims through loyalty to the caliph sultan, was an impossibility, he claimed. The Ottomans did not rule over all Muslims, who were divided among competing empires. He concluded that the only viable political strategy was the ‘creation of a Turkish political nation based on race’ and the unification of the primarily Muslim Turkic peoples, including those beyond the Ottoman borders in the Caucasus and Russia. Nationalism would be the determining force of the future.
